Customer requested SOC2 docs and a short tracing benchmark using sample traffic; agreed next steps and POC scoping meeting.
topics: Error analysis and root cause workflows
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Aurelia CTO), Lisa Martinez (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Park (Platform), Priya Nair (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Samir Gupta: Samir here, CTO at Aurelia. We're looking at options for serving LLM features in our clinical workflows. Main concerns are latency, traceability, and strict audit requirements.
[00:22] Lisa Martinez: Hi, Lisa, ML lead. We're interested in how Redwood helps debug failures — like 500 errors, model timeouts, and when downstream services fail.
[00:33] Jordan Park: Jordan, platform. I'll be focused on logs, retention, and VPC connectivity.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Great, thanks. Ravi is our SE, he'll demo the console tracing and error analysis flows.
[00:43] Ravi Patel: Hey folks. Quick agenda: show tracing UI, correlate traces to request logs and full payloads, show error aggregation and root cause workflow, and touch on RBAC/audit and private deployment notes.

[01:05] Ravi Patel: (screen share) So starting in Console -> Traces, you get a timeline view. Each trace is a request across the stack; we capture routing, model variant, region, and any fallback events.
[01:20] Lisa Martinez: Sorry, are you capturing KV cache hits in traces? We do a lot of caching at prefix level.
[01:26] Ravi Patel: We do capture cache hit/miss metadata as part of the span. It's labeled Cache: HIT or MISS, although the transcription sometimes shows "K V cache" as separate words — bear with me.
[01:36] [01:40] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[01:42] Ravi Patel: Example trace — here's a single user request that hit a cold path then fell back to a quantized variant. You can expand spans to see timings: model inference, tokenization, routing, and external webhook calls.

[02:15] Maya Chen: One thing Aurelia asked previously was how to find the raw request/response for a given user — can you show that?
[02:21] Ravi Patel: Yep. Click into the trace, there's a Request Logs tab. That shows the original prompt, model inputs, response tokens, and metadata like request_id and user_id (if you pass it). We also stream the response so you can replay the output.
[02:36] Samir Gupta: How do you handle PII? We can't keep raw patient text unencrypted in logs for more than X days.
[02:44] Ravi Patel: Great question. We support configurable retention at the tenant level and can redact fields by key before storage. For Private deployments you control the KMS and can enable envelope encryption — logs at rest are encrypted. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs after.

[03:12] Lisa Martinez: When there's an error like a model OOM or a 502, how do you surface root cause?
[03:18] Ravi Patel: Two parts: error aggregation and trace-level diagnostics. In the Errors dashboard we roll up errors by type (timeout, OOM, network). Click an error type to see example traces and the common stack spans.
[03:33] [03:35] Speaker 2: can you repeat the timeout bit?
[03:36] Ravi Patel: Sure — timeout errors show the percentiles and example traces. For a single trace you can inspect the exact span where the latency spike occurred and jump to the corresponding request log. If the runtime retried or fell back to another model, that is recorded as a child span.

[04:05] Jordan Park: Does the trace include infra metrics? Like GPU memory, host-level OOM logs?
[04:12] Ravi Patel: We surface GPU memory usage and queue depths as span tags when available. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can ingest host-level metrics into the trace UI — often our runtime emits those metrics. If you need full host logs we can integrate with your log forwarder or ship an export.

[04:40] Maya Chen: Quick demo of a debugging flow. Ravi — pick a failure and walk through it.
[04:45] Ravi Patel: Ok, here's a 502 spike. On the trace timeline you see multiple requests failing at the model inference span. I open one trace: the model returned an error code that maps to OOM on the runtime. Request log shows truncated output, and the trace notes a fallback to a lower-memory variant — you can see the fallback span and its duration.
[05:12] Lisa Martinez: Does Redwood auto-retry or do we configure that?
[05:16] Ravi Patel: You can configure retry policies per route: max retries, backoff, and whether to do transparent fallback to a compatible model variant. We recommend limited retries for idempotent calls only.

[05:35] Samir Gupta: We have concerns about correlating user identifiers across systems — how do you link traces to our internal user IDs without leaking?
[05:44] Ravi Patel: We support passing an opaque user_id or request_id that you control. We recommend hashing or tokenizing PII before sending. On the console we show the ID you pass; we can also map to your internal IDs if you provide a reversible mapping in a private deployment.

[06:10] [06:12] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[06:15] Ravi Patel: Also want to show Bulk Search — you can search logs by request_id, model, status, or custom tags. For wide-scale issues we link to the Alerts page and to the traces.

[06:40] Lisa Martinez: If we run an end-to-end test traffic through Redwood, can we replay requests for debugging?
[06:46] Ravi Patel: Yes — the Request Replay tool lets you re-run a request against a pinned model version or a canary variant. We capture the original env, headers, and inputs. For privacy we can disable replay in hosted mode or only allow it in Private deployments.

[07:10] Maya Chen: Let's talk about speed: when an engineer opens a trace, how long to load full logs and payloads?
[07:16] Ravi Patel: Usually sub-second for trace metadata and a few seconds for full log payloads depending on retention tier. We stream payloads incrementally so UI feels responsive even for large requests.

[07:35] Samir Gupta: How do you handle sampling? We can't store full traces for 100% traffic.
[07:42] Ravi Patel: Sampling policies are configurable: tail-sampling for errors, probabilistic sampling for normal traffic, or policy-based (e.g., sample 100% of requests with error status). You can also export sampled raw logs to your S3 for long-term retention.

[08:05] Priya Nair: From a security/audit lens, does Console record admin actions? We need audit trails that show who viewed logs and when.
[08:14] Ravi Patel: Yes — Console has audit logs for UI actions and API calls. We log who accessed a trace, who exported logs, and who changed RBAC. In Private deployments these audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.

[08:35] Lisa Martinez: You mentioned trace->log correlation IDs — what's the format?
[08:40] Ravi Patel: We use request_id and trace_id; both are UUIDs by default. We also allow you to inject your correlation id and we'll index it for search.

[09:00] [09:05] Speaker 1: (mumble)
[09:10] Ravi Patel: Next, error analysis: The platform surfaces anomaly detection on output quality and latency regressions. For example, if a new model rollout increases 95th latency by 30%, we'll flag it and attach sample traces.

[09:38] Samir Gupta: With rollouts — can we do canary and auto-fallback if quality drops?
[09:44] Ravi Patel: Yes, rollouts have guardrails: you can set SLOs for latency and quality metrics and the system can automatically revert if thresholds are violated. It can also route to a fallback model or Dedicated pool.

[10:05] Jordan Park: For Dedicated/Private, how are logs stored? Are they in our VPC?
[10:12] Ravi Patel: In Private deployment logs remain in your VPC/storage if you choose. For Redwood Dedicated it's tenant-isolated storage but managed by Redwood. We provide encryption at rest and in transit; you control KMS for Private.

[10:30] Maya Chen: (shares link) I'm dropping a short doc with a tracing checklist in chat.

[10:40] Ravi Patel: Now a quick walkthrough of the trace detail: expanding a span shows tags, attached events, and an optional stacktrace when the runtime throws an exception. Sometimes service names are transcribed weirdly — you'll see "red hood runtime" in transcripts occasionally, that's our runtime.

[11:05] Lisa Martinez: The stack traces — are they sanitized? We can't have internal PII or stack frames that leak code info.
[11:12] Ravi Patel: We can sanitize stack traces and redact filepaths. For hosted mode we sanitize by default; for Private you control verbosity.

[11:30] [11:35] Speaker 2: (laugh)
[11:38] Ravi Patel: Also going to demo a multi-request trace where a request fans out to a few downstream services: you can collapse or filter spans to focus on model inference only.

[12:05] Samir Gupta: Can we attach our ticket ID in the trace so SREs can jump from issue to trace?
[12:12] Ravi Patel: Absolutely — we support custom tags and annotations — you can call the API to annotate traces with your ticket keys.

[12:30] Maya Chen: Walk through a recent customer bug — quick case study?

[12:34] Ravi Patel: Customer X had intermittent 503s; trace showed a webhook span timing out because their downstream service throttled; the request log showed repeated retries. We surfaced the trend in Errors dashboard and recommended increasing webhook timeouts and enabling circuit breaking. The customer set a sampling rule to capture 100% of webhook failures and that helped root cause in 2 hours.

[13:10] Lisa Martinez: Nice. Regarding retention costs — if we increase sampling for errors will that spike bill?
[13:16] Maya Chen: It can; Redwood Optimize suggests sampling configurations and will estimate cost impact before you flip it. We'll include a cost estimate in the security pack.

[13:35] Jordan Park: About integrations — do you export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin or metrics to Prometheus?
[13:41] Ravi Patel: We support exporting traces via OTLP to your observability stack and metrics to Prometheus pushgateway or remote write. For logs we can forward to your S3/Splunk/Datadog.

[14:00] Priya Nair: SSO and RBAC — can we map to Okta groups and restrict view/edit rights on a per-route basis?
[14:08] Ravi Patel: Yes — SAML/Okta supported, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC at route/model/console level. You can configure who can view raw request payloads separately from who can view aggregated metrics.

[14:35] [14:40] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[14:42] Maya Chen: We're about halfway. Ravi any other demo pieces?

[14:48] Ravi Patel: I'll show the Alerts -> Diagnostics flow: Alerts link directly to a set of traces and suggested runbooks we maintain. If the alert is a latency spike, diagnostics page suggests looking at model variant CPU/GPU times and queue depths.

[15:20] Samir Gupta: If we onboard to Dedicated, can we run a private tracer endpoint?
[15:26] Ravi Patel: Yes, Dedicated and Private can host the tracing collector inside your VPC; you control the endpoint and retention.

[15:40] Lisa Martinez: Can Redwood's tracing connect to our distributed tracing so we have a single pane?
[15:46] Ravi Patel: We can inject the trace_id into headers so your services can include our trace_id in their spans. Then use OTLP export to merge traces in your tracing backend.

[16:05] Maya Chen: Let's show a failure reproduction using Request Replay — Ravi?
[16:10] Ravi Patel: Sure. I pick a failed trace, hit Replay against a pinned model. Replay shows same inputs; we can toggle configurations like batch size, quantization profile, and see if it reproduces. For this example, increasing batch size caused OOM; the replay reproduces that and shows the exact span where memory spikes.

[16:45] Jordan Park: We may want automatic anomaly detection on semantic quality — false positives are a worry. How tunable is that?
[16:52] Ravi Patel: Quality monitors are tied to evals and prompt sets. You configure evaluation thresholds and sample size; we surface drift and give suggested baselines. It's tunable and you can mute noisy alerts.

[17:15] Maya Chen: Quick security plug — Maya: we'll send the compliance pack and a suggested POC scope. Samir anything else?

[17:22] Samir Gupta: Would like to run a 2-week POC, sampling 5% traffic with tracing on, and run a tracer benchmark. Also need to see SOC2 and encryption model.

[17:32] Maya Chen: Noted. Ravi, can you run a short tracing benchmark with their sample traffic?

[17:36] Ravi Patel: Yes — ask Samir to share a week's traffic window and we'll run it in a dedicated test pool.

[17:44] Lisa Martinez: One last question: if a model update causes quality regression, how quickly can we roll back in the Console?
[17:50] Ravi Patel: Canary rollouts are immediate — you can pin a previous model version and route 100% back within seconds. The Console shows commit history per route.

[18:10] [18:12] Speaker 1: (mumble)
[18:15] Maya Chen: Ok, let's recap next steps.

[18:18] Maya Chen: 1) Maya to send SOC2 + security pack. 2) Samir to share sample traffic and request logs. 3) Ravi to schedule and run trace benchmark and demo replay. 4) Schedule POC scoping on 2025-04-21.

[18:40] Samir Gupta: Sounds good. Appreciate the walkthrough.

[18:44] Lisa Martinez: Thanks, that was useful.

[18:47] Priya Nair: We'll review the security pack when you send it.

[18:50] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up in email. Thanks everyone.

[19:00] (meeting ends — transcript may be missing some filler words and there are occasional transcription errors; refer to recording for exact audio)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "K V cache" for KV cache, "red hood runtime" mis-transcription of runtime name. References shared in chat: tracing-checklist.pdf (link), SOC2_summary.pdf (link), sample-benchmark-params.xlsx (link).
